newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai grains market quiet, quota meeting watched.
newsitem.headline: Thai grains market quiet, quota meeting watched.

text.p: The Thai grains and oilseeds market was quiet this week amid softer Chicago futures as players were sidelined on expectations of further price drops, traders said on Tuesday.
A major lead in the market was a forthcoming government meeting which could lead to the removal of import quota on products used in the export industry, including corn.
"We heard there is a good chance that the import quota on corn will be removed," said one industry source.
The meeting, to be held on Wednesday, follows an export summit held late last month on boosting competitiveness of Thai exports.
Exporters claim import quotas raise their production costs.
At present, the government sets import quotas for corn each year depending on the local supply situation. This year the quota was set at 200,000 tonnes but feed producers claimed it was not enough.
There were not many other developments in the market, traders said.

"With Chicago prices heading down, there is not much incentive to jump into the market now. Two companies were said to have bid but did not buy," said one trader with a US trading firm. "Besides, many have covered their short-term demand."
"Players are waiting to see how low the price will go. Once prices edge up, buyers will enter the market,' he added.
Local soymeal was mixed around 9.75-9.80 baht a kg from 9.55-9.90 baht ($0.36) a week earlier. Corn prices dropped to 4.60 baht from 4.80 a week earlier.
Traders said they heard about the cancelled Cargill zinc for wheat deal in North Korea but did not hear that the 20,000 tonnes of wheat was heading for Thailand.
